source_title: If INDIAN COLLEGES can’t secure even ₹25K/month jobs after 4 years of B.Tech CSE, they should start REFUNDING tuition. Let’s stop sugarcoating it. B.Tech CSE graduates in India are being cheated. After 4 years of grinding, outdated syllabi, 75% attendan - LinkedIn
source_excerpt:
If INDIAN COLLEGES can’t secure even ₹25K/month jobs after 4 years of B.Tech CSE, they should start REFUNDING tuition. Let’s stop sugarcoating it. B.Tech CSE graduates in India are being cheated. After 4 years of grinding, outdated syllabi, 75% attendance, forced internships, and sleepless nights building final-year projects, they step into a market offering ₹15K–₹25K/month. Sometimes for full-time work. Sometimes for free in the name of “exposure.” Meanwhile, someone who took a 3-month Full Stack bootcamp is offered ₹50K–₹1L/month in Bangalore. That’s not a skill gap. That’s a system failure. Colleges charge lakhs in fees but teach nothing about real-world tech stacks, open-source, interviews, freelancing, or salary negotiation. Companies exploit freshers as cheap labor. And universities? Just hand out degrees and celebrate outdated placement stats. If a ₹6L-₹12L degree can’t even pay for rent and groceries, what exactly are we paying for? Prestige? Passion? Poverty? No one blames CSE students for jumping to UI/UX, product, or even digital marketing. It’s not betrayal. It’s survival. It’s self-respect. The industry won’t fix itself until we call it out. If you’re a young engineer earning less than a Swiggy delivery partner, you’re not the problem. The system is. #BtechCSE #Engineering #Freshers #TechJobs #PayGap #IndianEducation #JobSearch #CampusToCorporate
This is the real story. 4 years. 8 semesters. 60+ exams. 100+ assignments. Lakhs in fees. And at the end, interviewer asks: "Do you know React? We need React." College taught us how to clear exams, not how to clear interviews. The problem is not students. The problem is a system where degree is 4 years old but industry moves every 4 months. If colleges can't get even 25k jobs after B.Tech CSE, refund is not the solution, reform is. Teach skills, not just syllabus.
The frustrating part is that students are often told to get a degree, build projects, complete internships, and learn skills, yet many still struggle to get their first real opportunity. Colleges should be accountable for how well they prepare students for industry, not just how many degrees they award. At the same time, companies need to stop expecting freshers to have years of experience before giving them a chance to prove themselves. The real question is whether education is preparing students for the jobs that actually exist today.

Raunak Yadush 5mo Edited Report this post AI is changing the entire vibe of coding. A few years ago, developers were judged by how fast they could write code. Now? The real power is shifting toward: • problem solving • system thinking • creativity • product vision • decision making AI can already generate code. Soon it will generate entire applications. But here’s what most people still don’t understand: The future developer is not someone who competes WITH AI. The future developer is someone who thinks THROUGH AI. The era of “syntax memorization” is dying. The era of: “build faster than everyone else” has begun. And honestly? Your degree alone will matter less and less. Because AI doesn’t care: • which college you came from • what your GPA was • whether you are Tier 1 or Tier 3 AI rewards people who can: • learn fast • adapt fast • build fast The internet is becoming the biggest equalizer. A teenager with AI tools and internet access can now compete with experienced engineers. That changes everything. I believe the next generation of engineers will look very different. One person with AI tools will build what previously needed: • 10 developers • 5 designers • 3 marketers • a full support team We are entering the age of solo billion-dollar companies. And this excites me more than it scares me. Because AI is not replacing ambitious people. It is amplifying them. The biggest mistake developers can make right now is: acting like AI is temporary. It’s not temporary. It’s the new infrastructure layer of the internet. Soon every company will become an AI company. Every app will have AI inside it. Every workflow will be automated. The question is no longer: “Will AI replace developers?” The real question is: “Will developers who ignore AI survive?” As an AI developer, here’s what I think we need to focus on now: 1. Learn how AI models actually work Not just prompting. Understand: • transformers • embeddings • fine-tuning • agents • inference • vector databases • multimodal systems 2. Build real products The future belongs to builders. Not tutorial collectors. 3. Learn AI as early as possible Don’t wait for college to teach you. Most universities are already behind industry. 4. Master communication AI writes code. Humans still sell vision. 5. Become insanely adaptable Technology cycles are becoming shorter every year. 6. Focus on execution speed Ideas are cheap now. Execution is everything. My prediction? In the next 5 years: • AI copilots will become mandatory • Traditional coding interviews will decline • Small AI-native teams will outperform huge companies • Developers will manage AI systems instead of manually coding everything • The line between developer, founder, and creator will disappear And the people building with AI today will define the next decade. The future will not belong to people who fear AI. It will belong to people who learn faster than everyone else. 2,549 103 Comments Like Comment Share Copy LinkedIn Facebook X To view or add a comment, sign in
